title: Northlight claims edge probe log
content:
Context / call summary:
- 2025-04-08 sync with Northlight Insurance engineering + product (45m). Goal: quick feasibility check for integrating Redwood inference into their claims triage flow (first-pass classification + summary generation).
- Attendees: Priya (Rwd SE), Diego (Rwd infra lead), Hannah (Rwd solutions), Mark Ellis (Northlight eng lead), Sara Gupta (product), Tom Reed (security).

High-level ask from Northlight:
- Route incoming claims (text + attachments metadata) through an LLM endpoint to: (A) classify severity & routing, (B) extract structured fields (policy id, incident date), (C) generate an initial summary for human reviewers.
- Hard constraints: P95 latency <= 600ms for light text-only requests (90% of traffic). Heavy requests (OCR + long descriptions) can be async with SLA 30s.
- Data/privacy: PHI not expected but PII present; must support VPC/private deploy and KMS integration for keys and audit logs.
- Availability: multi-region failover preferred (US-East primary, US-West secondary).

Notes from technical discussion:
- Model choice: they want a >open-source model (reasonable quality) and quantized for cost. Recommended: start with small-proof model (gpt-xyz-13b-qlora) for prototype, then evaluate Redwood-verified variants.
- Deployment mode: Private (VPC) with control plane in Redwood and inference inside customer VPC via private connectors OR fully customer-hosted package depending on security sign-off. We flagged Dedicated-reserved as intermediate option but they want no data egress.
- KV cache behavior: important for repeated identical prefixes (claim templates). Suggested: enable prefix KV caching with TTL 2h initially, monitor cache hit rate. Note: prefix caching reduces cost but can alter prompt-context semantics if templates evolve rapidly.
- Batching/concurrency: workload will be bursty (end-of-day filing). Recommend conservative max_batch_size of 8, target batch window 8-12ms to balance latency/cost.
- Fallbacks: define model fallback policy -> smaller quantized model for degraded capacity & region fallback to Redwood-hosted only if customer accepts egress (they currently do not).
- Security: must integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS) for model-serving keys and audit logs to their SIEM. They want HSM discussion for later.
- Observability: require per-route latency/cost traces and token-level cost for initial 90d. We can provide rollups via Redwood Console + exported traces to Datadog.

Gotchas / open risks flagged on call:
- Attachments (images): OCR pipeline not in scope for v1. If they add OCR, that will push the request size and may need async job + S3 staging.
- Tokenization/field extraction edge cases: policy numbers in many formats; need curated prompt set + eval suite to avoid regressions.
- Rate limits: they plan a 3rd-party UI that can fan out many small requests; need to set per-token quotas and route-level throttles. Also discuss client-side retries/backoff to avoid thundering herd.
- Model quantization quality: some enterprise reviewers noted hallucination risk with aggressively quantized weights. Plan explicit quality gates before rollouts.
- Network egress policy: Northlight's security is currently a block on any external endpoints. That pushes toward fully private deployment or on-prem package. Procurement timeline for that is 6–8 weeks.

Preliminary evaluation plan (MVP):
1) Prototype endpoint (2-week spike): deploy a private-limited cluster in their VPC with a conservative model. Run dataset of 1k historical claims (anonymized) to measure P95 latency, cost per 1k requests, and extraction accuracy. (Owner: Diego).
2) Prompt/eval harness: build 50 focused prompts + golden labels for key fields (policy id, date, claimant name, severity). Integrate Redwood Optimize suggestions after first run. (Owner: Hannah).
3) Observability + alerting: wire initial dashboards, set regression alert on extraction F1 drop of >3%. (Owner: Priya).
4) Security sign-off: produce architecture diagram for Northlight security review (including KMS flows, VPC peering, no public IP). (Owner: Priya/Hannah).

Recommended config snippet (proto notes, not config file):
- deployment_mode: private-vpc
- region_priority: [us-east1, us-west1]
- instance_profile: g5-16 (start w/ 2 nodes), autoscale: min 1 / max 6
- model_profile: quantized-13b-low-latency
- batching: max_batch_size 8, batch_ms 10
- caching: prefix_kv_cache: enabled, ttl: 7200s
- observability: export_traces: datadog://northlight-claims, metrics_retention: 90d

Next steps / action items (with tentative dates):
- Diego: prototype infra build (VPC skeleton, basic endpoint) — aim to have PoC running by 2025-04-25.
- Hannah: collect 1k anonymized claims dataset + write initial 50 eval prompts — due 2025-04-18.
- Priya: architecture diagram + security checklist to send to Northlight security (include KMS flows) — send by 2025-04-16.
- Mark (Northlight): confirm legal/POLICY stance on external cloud endpoints OR provide contact for procurement to discuss private package procurement timeline — update by 2025-04-20.
- All: schedule follow-up deep-dive (90m) to review PoC metrics and quality. Proposed: 2025-04-28.

Notes-to-self / conversation fragments to capture:
- "If they can't allow any egress we should position the on-prem box as a stop-gap — still needs infra ops commitment from them."
- Consider building a small anonymization shim that strips PII client-side before sending requests to any hosted variant; helps unblock early tests while procurement proceeds.
- Watch for claims with long transcripts (>2k tokens) — need explicit async flow + storage.

Questions for internal follow-up:
- What recent Redwood quantized models have known extraction hallucination rates? Any internal bench on 13b-qlora vs 7b-int8 for structured extraction? (Ask research/applied-ml).
- Do we have a quick script to seed prefix KV cache with common claim templates for better cold-start behavior? (Ask serving-runtime).

Meeting artifacts / links to create:
- Confluence page: CLM / Northlight integration (create and link CONFLUENCE-4337)
- Jira epic: JIRA-CLM-221 (prototype branch and infra tickets)
- Git branch: private-deploy/nd-claims-proxy (seed with config above)

Quick triage checklist to bring to PoC run:
- [ ] confirm dataset anonymization (PHI/PII removal)
- [ ] baseline eval scripts + golden labels
- [ ] KV cache TTL and monitoring dashboard
- [ ] fallback model variant defined and smoke-tested
- [ ] rate-limiting policy for UI integrations

End of notes.

(Keeping this in users/ as a working journal — update after PoC bootstrapped.)
